In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the introduction of a phenylphosphonated moiety into the acyclic nucleosides does not significantly influence their cytostatic activity.
the cytostatic activity is not correlated with the pKa values of arylphosphates, but with the hydrophobicity of the substituents.
the introduction of the arylphosphonyl moiety into the acyclic phosphonate nucleosides is not advantageous in terms of the cytostatic or antiviral activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2-(purin-9-yl)ethoxyarylphosphonates are a novel class of acyclic nucleosides with interesting biological properties.
the cytostatic and anti-HIV-1 activity of the compounds was generally higher than that of the corresponding arylphosphonic acid.
the cytostatic activities of the target arylphosphonic acids are comparable or even better than those of the parent nucleosides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a phenyl group in the side-chain of the acyclic nucleosides is not detrimental to their biological properties.

the pKa of a phosphonate moiety can be significantly influenced by the presence of a phenolic hydroxyl group in the molecule, and that such influence is strongly dependent on the position of the hydroxyl group relative to the phosphonate.
the presence of the arylphosphonyl group in the molecule is not sufficient for the expression of cytostatic and anti-HIV activity.
